question: Should `talk.idleTimeoutS` govern every configured macOS Talk session, or only Talk sessions started by Voice Wake?
rationale: The canonical issue is specifically about handing control back after Voice Wake, but the proposed runtime has no activation-source distinction and applies the setting to manually started Talk sessions as well; this permanent public contract requires owner intent.

options.title: Limit to Voice Wake sessions
options.body: Carry the activation source into the Talk lifecycle and apply idle expiry only to Voice Wake-started sessions, matching the reported workflow and avoiding changed manual-session semantics.

options.title: Apply to all Talk sessions
options.body: Keep the simpler general opt-in contract and explicitly document that manually started Talk also expires when configured.

options.title: Do not add the config
options.body: Defer or close the PR if maintainers prefer existing manual-stop behavior over another public Talk setting.

recommendation.title: Limit to Voice Wake sessions
recommendation.body: Carry the activation source into the Talk lifecycle and apply idle expiry only to Voice Wake-started sessions, matching the reported workflow and avoiding changed manual-session semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Merged history ties this person to the unified Talk runtime and gateway-session architecture that define the behavior and public contract.
